handoff.salientSummary: Round 1 user testing of milestone "foundation": 21 of 24 assertions pass, 3 fail (VAL-FND-006, VAL-FND-009, VAL-FND-024). Two of the failures are already-known deferred scrutiny items; VAL-FND-006 is new (four contract-named capacity rules are implemented nowhere). 7 flow validators ran; synthesis and validation-state.json are written.
handoff.whatWasImplemented: Ran the full user-testing validation for milestone "foundation" across 7 flow-validator groups (terminal/Vitest, sqlite reads, agent-browser on App 3001, curl on App internal routes). Started the App dev server, verified tenant-api US/KSA health, verified flag/permission DB state, wrote Flow Validator Guidance sections plus 9 runtime findings into library/user-testing.md, produced 7 flow reports with evidence under evidence/foundation/<group>/, wrote validation/foundation/user-testing/synthesis.json, and updated validation-state.json for VAL-FND-001..024 (21 passed, 3 failed, 0 blocked). Stopped the App and closed all browser sessions; the repo tree is clean.
handoff.whatWasLeftUndone: No fixes applied (validation only). VAL-FND-006, VAL-FND-009 and VAL-FND-024 remain failed and need either a fix feature or an orchestrator waiver. Sites (3008) and Admin (3005) were not exercised because no foundation assertion needs them. VAL-FND-011/012's criteria were verified against a fresh temp DB built from the migration; the stale KSA local tenant DB trigger bodies (known deferred item) were re-confirmed but are not part of those criteria.

tests.coverage: No tests were added or changed (validation-only feature). The round ran the existing suites: @repo/zoned-time 11, @repo/staffing 634, @repo/reservations 65, @repo/auth 30, @repo/tenant-db reservations-schema 6, tenant-api auth/routing/write/context/security suites, App token/role-presets/guards suites — all exit 0. Coverage gaps found inside those suites are recorded as discovered issues (validateConfig combination codes; staff_only/unavailable mode exclusions; property run seeds).

discoveredIssues.description: VAL-FND-006: four capacity rules the contract names are enforced nowhere — rsv_service_availability.online_cap_per_interval, rsv_service_availability.concurrent_covers_cap, rsv_pacing_rules.rolling_min/rolling_max_covers and rsv_tables.reset_buffer_min are referenced only by the schema (plus the seed script and the schema test), and the engine's input models have no fields for them (only the location-level settings.bufferMin is applied). Invariant I3's overbook semantics are also unmet: OccupancyIndex skips overbook rows in every lookup (engine/occupancy.ts:94,127,139,165) though architecture.md:225-227 requires overbook rows to count as occupying their tables; the test oracle skips them too, so nothing catches it.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Extend EnginePacingRuleInput/EngineServiceAvailabilityInput/EngineTableInput with the rolling-window, concurrent-cover, per-interval online-cap and per-table reset-buffer fields, enforce them in searchAvailability/planBooking (guest channels filtered, staff channels warned), make overbook rows consume their table's capacity for guest availability per architecture I3, widen alternatives() to return { sameDay, otherDates } per architecture.md:1181, and add tests for each rule.

discoveredIssues.description: VAL-FND-009: the property suite runs green but does not verify I1-I8 with the contract/architecture semantics — no search→hold agreement, monotonic release, atomic modify or staff-overbook isolation check; the oracle attaches I6/I7/I8 labels to pacing caps, channel/mode eligibility and service-window checks (testing/oracle.ts:76-199,229-261), and the oracle comparison runs once per scenario rather than per step. This is the same gap as scrutiny round-2 blocking issue #2, already folded into foh-setup-full-stack.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: As in scrutiny issue #2: add the four missing per-step checks, relabel the oracle to one canonical invariant list, and map each invariant to its proving assertion.

discoveredIssues.description: VAL-FND-024: docs/decisions/048-reservations-data-residency.md covers 9 of the 11 topics the contract enumerates; 'guest identity without login' (capability/manage-link/OTP model) and the 'shared org alarm' (generic per-organization alarm running staff and reservations) have no content. Scrutiny also flagged secondary drift in the same docs (non-existent trigger names in section 5, '24 rsv_* tables' vs 41, implied-read rules, preset count).
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Add a short section on guest identity without login (HMAC capability tokens, manage links in the URL fragment, hashes only) and one on the shared per-org alarm (Durable Object alarm on Workers, interval on Node, staff + reservations modules) to ADR 048, and correct the drifted trigger names, table count and role-preset/implied-read statements.

discoveredIssues.description: The KSA local tenant DB packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db still carries pre-fix trigger bodies ('table_overlap' with no o.overbook = 0 filter; rsv_holds_single_conversion requiring OLD.status='converted' AND NEW.status='converted') while the US-dir DBs carry the corrected SQL. Re-confirmed read-only this round. Not part of VAL-FND-011/012 criteria (they build a fresh temp DB).
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: As in scrutiny issue #3, included in foh-setup-full-stack: DROP/CREATE the affected triggers from the 0016 SQL in the KSA DB and verify sqlite_master in both TENANT_DB_DIR roots.

discoveredIssues.description: Test-coverage gaps inside suites that otherwise pass: packages/reservations/src/config/config.test.ts never asserts combination_too_few_members, combination_uncombinable_table or the valid-config empty-issues case (verified only by invoking validateConfig directly); staff_only/unavailable mode exclusions are implemented (engine/day-state.ts:130-146) but have no direct assertion; passing property runs print no seed or fast-check counter, so a counterexample repro relies on FC_SEED.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Add the missing config assertions, a mode-exclusion test per channel, and enable fast-check verbose/seed logging (or record seeds in the test name) so failures are reproducible.
